# Larry James Henry

> Azure platform engineering, governance and DevOps for platform and cloud leads at banks and insurers, by Larry James Henry.

Last updated: 2026-10-30

About the author: [About Larry James Henry](https://larryjameshenry.com/about/)

## Architecting Real-World Web Apps using Local Qwen3.5 9B Models

- [The Architect's Guide to Building Web Apps with Local AI: OpenCode on an 8GB GPU](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/local-ai-opencode-guide/): A comprehensive guide to replacing cloud-based AI with a fully local stack (OpenCode, Qwen3.5 9B, Ollama) to architect and build a full-stack web app from scratch.
- [Scaffolding a Modern Frontend with OpenCode and Next.js](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/opencode-nextjs-frontend-scaffolding/): A focused guide on using the OpenCode terminal agent to generate a production-ready Next.js frontend and style it entirely offline using local AI.
- [Building Secure Backend APIs using Qwen3.5 9B](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/secure-backend-api-qwen/): Use the Qwen3.5 9B model via Ollama to design, write, and document an Express.js REST API offline, without shipping proprietary schemas to a cloud LLM.
- [Mastering Context: Configuring AGENTS.md for Web Projects](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/configuring-agents-md-web-projects/): Configure OpenCode's AGENTS.md to define architectural rules, coding standards, and persistent memory for your local AI on web projects.
- [Iterative Debugging: Fixing Hallucinations in 9B Local Agents](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/debugging-9b-agent-hallucinations/): Learn practical techniques for managing the agentic loop, identifying AI hallucinations, and fixing bugs iteratively with OpenCode.
- [Integrating MCP (Model Context Protocol) with OpenCode for Web Dev](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/integrating-mcp-opencode-web/): An advanced guide on extending OpenCode's capabilities by connecting it to external tools and databases using the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

## Azure DevOps YAML Expression Masterclass

- [The Ultimate Guide to Azure DevOps YAML Expressions: Never Fail a Condition Again](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/ultimate-guide-yaml-expressions/): How Azure DevOps evaluates ${{ }}, $[ ] and $( ), and how to write pipeline conditions that hold up across governed, multi-team CI/CD platforms.
- [Debugging Silent Pipeline Failures: When your if Statement Evaluates to Null](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/debugging-silent-pipeline-failures/): Why a compile-time ${{ if }} can't see runtime variables in Azure DevOps, how to find the silent failures it causes, and the patterns that fix them.
- [Escaping Parameter Hell: Architectural Patterns for Nested Templates](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/escaping-parameter-hell/): Pass data through five layers of Azure DevOps templates without redeclaring parameters, and keep typed validation where teams call your templates.
- [templateContext Deep Dive: Bundling Metadata with Jobs and Stages](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/templatecontext-deep-dive/): Attach owner and security-tier metadata to Azure DevOps jobs with templateContext, without letting a team's own label switch off a required control.
- [Advanced each Looping: Iterating Through Complex Nested Objects](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/advanced-each-looping-iterating-complex-nested-objects/): Loop over nested objects with ${{ each }} in Azure DevOps to generate stages, jobs and steps for multi-region deployments without copy-pasted YAML.
- [Dynamic Matrix Strategies: Generating Runtime Tests with ${{ each }}](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/dynamic-matrix-test-strategies/): Combine compile-time ${{ each }} loops with runtime matrix strategies in Azure DevOps to generate large parallel test suites from one YAML parameter.
- [Cross-Job Communication: Mastering dependencies and Output Variables](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/cross-job-communication-mastering-dependencies-output-variables/): Pass output variables between Azure DevOps jobs and stages with dependencies and stageDependencies, and avoid the syntax mistakes that return empty.
- [Expression Security: Preventing Injection and Hardening Your YAML](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/expression-security-hardening/): Prevent expression injection in Azure DevOps YAML with typed parameters and safe input handling, and use required template checks to enforce it.
- [Solving Initialization Lag: Optimizing Expression Evaluation Speed](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/solving-initialization-lag/): Why large Azure DevOps pipelines take 45 seconds or more to start, what the expansion phase is doing, and how to restructure templates to cut the wait.

## Azure Platform Engineering: Build an Enterprise Landing Zone from Scratch

- [Azure Platform Engineering: The Complete Guide to Building an Enterprise Landing Zone](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/azure-landing-zone-guide/): Build an Azure landing zone you can defend to security and audit: management groups, hub-spoke, PIM, policy as code, and how to choose Terraform or Pulumi.
- [Design Your Azure Management Group and Subscription Hierarchy](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/azure-management-group-design/): Design and deploy a production Azure management group hierarchy with Terraform AVM and Pulumi. Covers intermediate groups, platform vs workload separation, and subscription placement.
- [Hub-and-Spoke Networking for Azure Landing Zones: Azure Firewall, Bastion, and Private DNS](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/azure-hub-spoke-networking/): Build a production hub-and-spoke network for Azure landing zones. Covers Azure Firewall Premium, Bastion scaling, DNS Private Resolver, and VNet peering with gateway transit.
- [Identity and Access Architecture for Azure Landing Zones: Entra ID, RBAC, and PIM](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/azure-identity-architecture/): Design the identity layer of an Azure landing zone. Covers Entra ID vs Azure RBAC, Privileged Identity Management (PIM), and secret-less OIDC authentication for GitHub Actions.
- [Governance at Scale: Writing and Deploying Azure Policies with Terraform and Pulumi](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/azure-policy-governance/): Azure Policy as code with Terraform and Pulumi: Deny and DeployIfNotExists, least-privilege remediation, exemptions, and compliance evidence an auditor accepts.
- [Subscription Vending: Automating New Workload Onboarding with IaC](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/azure-subscription-vending/): Automate Azure subscription vending with a PR-based workflow: spoke networking, RBAC and budgets at birth, plus an approval trail you can hand to audit.
- [Centralized Monitoring: Log Analytics, Diagnostic Settings, and Azure Monitor Workbooks](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/azure-monitor-logging/): Centralized logging for an Azure landing zone: Log Analytics workspace design, retention auditors ask for, DCR cost filtering, and diagnostic settings by policy.
- [Security Baseline: Defender for Cloud and Microsoft Sentinel in a Landing Zone](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/azure-security-baseline/): Deploy Defender for Cloud and Microsoft Sentinel at management group scope, and turn Secure Score into regulatory compliance evidence your auditors will accept.
- [CI/CD Pipeline for Your Landing Zone: Deploying Azure Verified Modules with GitHub Actions](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/azure-landing-zone-cicd/): A landing zone pipeline with GitHub Actions: OIDC instead of secrets, policy checks, protected state, and separation of duties that stands up as a change record.
- [Cost Governance in the Landing Zone: Tagging Enforcement, Budgets, and FinOps Automation](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/azure-landing-zone-costs/): Azure cost governance in the landing zone: enforced tags, forecast budget alerts, anomaly detection, and a chargeback model for shared platform costs.
- [Day-2 Operations: Maintaining and Evolving Your Azure Landing Zone](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/azure-landing-zone-ops/): Run an Azure landing zone after go-live: weekly drift detection, when to revert versus accept a manual change, RBAC reviews, and safe migration to AVM.

## Privacy-First AI DevOps on Azure

- [The Ultimate Guide to Secure AI DevOps on Azure: A Privacy-First Blueprint](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/the-ultimate-guide-to-secure-ai-devops-on-azure/): Adopt Azure OpenAI and GitHub Copilot with data controls security will sign off on: Private Link, keyless identity, zero data retention, and what to do first.
- [Configuring Azure OpenAI Private Link: Keeping AI Traffic Off the Public Internet](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/configuring-azure-openai-private-link/): Lock down Azure OpenAI with Private Endpoints, private DNS and public access disabled, and see why service endpoints and IP rules won't satisfy a security review.
- [Mastering Zero Data Retention: The Guide to Modified Abuse Monitoring in Azure OpenAI](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/mastering-zero-data-retention-modified-abuse-monitoring/): Eligibility criteria, application steps, and technical verification for Azure OpenAI Zero Data Retention via the Modified Abuse Monitoring program.
- [GitHub Copilot Enterprise Governance: Content Exclusions & Policy Controls](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/github-copilot-enterprise-governance-content-exclusions-policy-controls/): Govern GitHub Copilot Enterprise: server-side content exclusions, enterprise policies, EMU and audit streaming, and when to disable Copilot for a repo instead.
- [Keyless AI: Using Entra ID Managed Identities for Azure OpenAI](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/keyless-ai-entra-id-managed-identities-azure-openai/): Replace Azure OpenAI API keys with Entra ID Managed Identities and DefaultAzureCredential across VMs, AKS, Functions, and CI/CD pipelines.
- [Building a Secure RAG System for Internal DevOps Documentation](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/building-a-secure-rag-system-for-internal-devops-documentation/): Build a private DevOps knowledge base using Azure AI Search and Azure OpenAI with Private Link, Managed Identity, and document-level security trimming.
- [Securing the Prompt: Implementing AI Guardrails with Azure API Management](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/securing-the-prompt-ai-guardrails-azure-api-management/): Use Azure API Management as an AI gateway to sanitize prompts, detect PII and secrets, enforce token budgets, and audit AI traffic to your own Log Analytics workspace.
- [AI-Driven Secrets Scanning: Protecting the Pipeline from Hallucinated Credentials](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/ai-driven-secrets-scanning-protecting-pipeline-hallucinated-credentials/): Configure GHAS secret scanning, push protection, and Copilot Autofix to catch both real leaked secrets and AI-hallucinated credentials before they reach production.
- [The AI SRE Blueprint: Securely Automating Incident Response on Azure](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/the-ai-sre-blueprint-securely-automating-incident-response-on-azure/): Architect AI agents that autonomously investigate and remediate Azure incidents within least-privilege boundaries, with human-in-the-loop gates for production actions.
- [Continuous Compliance: Using AI to Generate and Audit Azure Policy](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/continuous-compliance-using-ai-to-generate-and-audit-azure-policy/): Use Azure OpenAI to draft custom Azure Policy definitions, audit IaC for compliance drift, and explain policy violations — all integrated into a GitOps CI/CD pipeline.

## The Local AI Coding Revolution: Getting Started with OpenCode

- [The Ultimate Guide to Local AI Coding with OpenCode and Ollama](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/ultimate-guide-local-ai-coding/): A comprehensive, end-to-end guide on moving from cloud-based AI assistants to a fully local, private, terminal-based AI coding stack using OpenCode.
- [Hardware & VRAM Guide for Local Code LLMs](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/hardware-vram-guide-local-code-llms/): A deep dive into the hardware requirements for local AI coding, focusing on VRAM, quantization (Q4_K_M), and the 8GB rule for 9B models.
- [Installing and Configuring Ollama for Code Generation](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/installing-configuring-ollama-code-generation/): A focused guide on setting up Ollama, pulling the best models for coding, and optimizing the Modelfile for context window management.
- [Mastering the OpenCode Terminal User Interface](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/mastering-opencode-tui/): A practical tutorial on installing OpenCode, navigating its TUI, and using slash commands to generate code and manage files directly from your terminal.
- [The Enterprise Case: Security and Privacy with Local AI](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/enterprise-case-security-privacy-local-ai/): An analysis of the data security benefits of local AI coding, explaining how keeping code off third-party servers solves major compliance headaches.

## The Shift-Left Container Security Playbook

- [The Ultimate Guide to Shift-Left Security for Docker Containers](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/shift-left-security-playbook/): A comprehensive, step-by-step playbook for integrating open-source security tools across the SDLC, from the IDE to the final CI/CD build gate.
- [Catching Mistakes Early: Setting Up Pre-Commit Hooks for Docker](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/pre-commit-hooks-docker/): A practical guide to using the pre-commit framework with tools like Trufflehog and Hadolint to block hardcoded secrets and bad Dockerfile practices.
- [Linting Infrastructure as Code: A Deep Dive into Checkov](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/linting-iac-checkov/): Learn how to use Checkov to automatically scan Dockerfiles and Kubernetes manifests for misconfigurations before they are deployed.
- [Integrating Trivy Vulnerability Scanning into GitHub Actions](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/trivy-github-actions/): A step-by-step tutorial on adding Trivy to a CI/CD pipeline to scan container images for OS and dependency vulnerabilities.
- [Beating Alert Fatigue: How to Filter and Prioritize Vulnerabilities](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/vulnerability-alert-fatigue/): Strategies for configuring open-source scanners to ignore irrelevant CVEs and prioritize what actually matters in your containers.
- [Hardening from the Ground Up: Using Distroless Base Images](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/distroless-base-images/): How switching from full OS base images to minimal distroless images drastically reduces your attack surface and pipeline scan times.

## Articles

- [How One Forgotten Pipeline Secret Deleted Production](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/forgotten-pipeline-secret-azure-post-mortem/): A forgotten GitHub Actions service principal deleted a healthcare portal, and missing blob read logs made it a HIPAA breach. Three Azure guardrails, in Pulumi.
- [The Best 7B and 8B Code Models in 2026, and Which Ones Security Will Approve](https://larryjameshenry.com/posts/best-8b-code-models-local-development/): Qwen3.5 9B, Gemma 4, DeepSeek-R1 Distill and Granite 4.1 compared on code quality, license and provenance, and where to run them so security will sign off.
